title: MedCaseAgent: From Multimodal Clinical Evidence to Rare Disease Case Reports
title_zh: MedCaseAgent：从多模态临床证据到罕见病病例报告

paragraphs.en: Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated potential in clinical documentation, generating the rigorous, evidence-based reasoning required for unprecedented, atypical, and rare disease case reports remains a significant challenge. We present MedCaseAgent, an end-to-end agentic reasoning paradigm that bridges this gap by synthesizing publication-quality reports from unstructured clinical notes. MedCaseAgent leverages a hierarchical structure, integrating patient-level data mining with iterative, tool-integrated reasoning. By dynamically querying medical literature and knowledge bases, the agent maintains high clinical fidelity and assesses case novelty. The framework is inherently modular, supporting various backbone LLMs in a plug-and-play fashion. To facilitate this research, we release MedCase-150K, a large-scale multimodal clinical case-report corpus, and MedCase-Bench, a robust temporally held-out evaluation suite. We also introduce an open-source model post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B and optimized specifically for this task. Under both LLM-judged and rule-based evaluation, MedCaseAgent outperforms existing general-purpose and specialized medical LLMs and agents. Blinded expert reviews and ablations further support the system’s clinical relevance and evidence grounding.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管大语言模型（LLMs）已在临床文档生成方面展现出潜力，但在生成针对前所未见、非典型及罕见疾病病例报告所需的严谨、基于证据的推理方面，仍然是一项重大挑战。 我们提出 MedCaseAgent，这是一种端到端的智能体推理范式，通过从非结构化临床笔记中综合生成达到发表质量的报告来弥合这一差距。 MedCaseAgent 采用分层结构，将患者级数据挖掘与迭代的、工具集成的推理相结合。 通过动态查询医学文献和知识库，智能体保持了高度的临床保真度并评估病例的新颖性。 该框架具有天然的模块化特性，支持以即插即用的方式使用各种骨干大语言模型。 为促进这一研究，我们发布了 MedCase-150K——一个大规模多模态临床病例报告语料库，以及 MedCase-Bench——一个采用时间外推划分的稳健评测套件。 我们还介绍了一个基于 Qwen3.5-9B 后训练并针对该任务专门优化的开源模型。 在大语言模型评审和基于规则的两种评估方式下，MedCaseAgent 均优于现有的通用及专业医学大语言模型和智能体。 盲法专家评审和消融实验进一步支持了该系统的临床相关性和证据依据。

paragraphs.en: A clinical case report, often referred to as a case study, is a comprehensive and highly structured account of a patient’s clinical encounter ( Cohen, 2006 ; Gagnier et al., 2014 ; Riley et al., 2017 ) . The defining characteristics of a compelling case report are its professionalism, novelty, and structural consistency. The presentation must be sufficiently rare, unique, or clinically significant to impart new medical knowledge. By publicly detailing these findings, case reports enable global medical communities to cross-reference phenotypically similar patients, accelerating the diagnosis of rare diseases, uncovering underlying molecular mechanisms, and facilitating larger-scale statistical analyses. Consequently, they serve as a vital cornerstone of medical progress, with nearly all top-tier medical journals dedicating specific categories to them and receiving a massive volume of global submissions. Despite their immense value, drafting these reports remains an arduous, entirely manual process for frontline physicians. Medical professionals must rigorously evaluate a case’s novelty, meticulously synthesize patient histories and treatment plans from fragmented raw clinical notes, and conduct extensive literature reviews to identify homologous cases or genetic loci. Ultimately, they face the heavy cognitive burden of integrating specialty-specific reasoning with rigorous scientific citations to complete the narrative.
paragraphs.zh: 临床病例报告，通常也称为个案研究，是对患者临床诊疗经历的一种全面且高度结构化的记述（Cohen, 2006；Gagnier et al., 2014；Riley et al., 2017）。 一份出色的病例报告的决定性特征在于其专业性、新颖性和结构一致性。 所呈现的病例必须足够罕见、独特或具有重要的临床意义，才能带来新的医学知识。 通过公开发表这些发现的详细内容，病例报告使全球医学界能够交叉比对表型相似的患者，从而加速罕见病的诊断、揭示潜在的分子机制，并促进更大规模的统计分析。 因此，病例报告构成了医学进步的重要基石，几乎所有顶级医学期刊都为其设立了专门的类别，并接收到来自全球的大量投稿。 尽管价值巨大，撰写这些报告对一线医生而言仍然是一个艰辛的、完全依赖人工的过程。 医学专业人员必须严格评估病例的新颖性，从零散的原始临床记录中细致地整合患者病史与治疗方案，并进行广泛的文献回顾，以识别同源病例或基因位点。 最终，他们还面临沉重的认知负担，需要将专科特有的推理与严谨的科学引用相结合，以完成报告的叙述。

paragraphs.en: Recent years have witnessed significant advancements in large language models (LLMs), with systems such as GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3.1 Pro exhibiting remarkable reasoning capabilities. While their proficiency in structured problem-solving and logical inference has positioned them as the central cognitive engines for various clinical diagnostic agents ( Chiu et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ) , these systems primarily focus on sequential diagnostic deduction rather than the generative synthesis of academic medical knowledge. Consequently, generating clinical case reports for rare diseases remains an exceptionally demanding frontier. It requires rigorous, multi-hop reasoning across highly fragmented and multimodal data streams, ranging from unstructured clinical shorthand and complex patient histories to rare imaging modalities and genomic sequences. Crucially, a viable case report generation pipeline must adhere to stringent factual constraints. It must strictly circumvent clinical hallucinations, such as spurious gene-literature matching, fabricated citations, or inaccurate patient summaries, which would entirely compromise the clinical validity of the report.
paragraphs.zh: 近年来，大型语言模型（LLMs）取得了显著进展，GPT-5.4 和 Gemini 3.1 Pro 等系统展现出了卓越的推理能力。 尽管它们在结构化问题求解和逻辑推断方面的能力使其成为各类临床诊断智能体的核心认知引擎（Chiu et al., 2025；Wang et al., 2025；Zhao et al., 2026），但这些系统主要侧重于序贯的诊断推演，而非学术医学知识的生成式综合。 因此，为罕见病生成临床病例报告仍然是一个极具挑战性的前沿方向。 这需要在高度碎片化的多模态数据流上进行严谨的多跳推理，这些数据流涵盖非结构化的临床速记、复杂的患者病史，以及罕见的影像学模态和基因组序列。 至关重要的是，一个可行的病例报告生成流程必须遵守严格的事实性约束。 它必须严格避免临床幻觉，例如虚假的基因-文献匹配、伪造的引用或不准确的患者摘要，因为这些会完全损害报告的临床有效性。

paragraphs.en: To address this gap, we propose MedCaseAgent, an end-to-end agentic framework that synthesizes academic-grade case reports from unstructured clinical notes. Structured as an interactive planner-writer-editor workflow, the agent orchestrates specialized tools for literature retrieval, exact citation tracking, image analysis, and genetic search to guarantee clinical accuracy and reduce hallucinations. In parallel, we construct MedCase-150K from over 7 million PubMed articles published since 2000 and derive MedCase-Bench as the recent held-out evaluation split. By automatically stratifying cases by clinical rarity, these resources provide a real-world simulation that tests how effectively models interpret fragmented multimodal evidence to formulate complete reports.
paragraphs.zh: 为弥补这一空白，我们提出 MedCaseAgent，这是一个端到端的智能体框架，能够从非结构化临床笔记中综合生成学术级别的病例报告。 该智能体采用交互式的规划器-撰写者-编辑者工作流结构，统筹专用工具进行文献检索、精确引用追踪、图像分析和基因搜索，以保证临床准确性并减少幻觉。 与此同时，我们从 2000 年以来发表的超过 700 万篇 PubMed 文章中构建了 MedCase-150K，并将其最近的留出评估部分派生为 MedCase-Bench。 通过按临床罕见程度对病例进行自动分层，这些资源提供了一个真实世界的模拟环境，用于测试模型解读碎片化多模态证据并撰写完整报告的能力。

paragraphs.en: Our contributions can be summarized as follows:
paragraphs.zh: 我们的贡献可以总结如下：

paragraphs.en: We propose MedCaseAgent , a plug-and-play clinical case report agent that integrates multimodal foundation models with dynamic tool-use mechanisms to actively orchestrate and synthesize complex clinical narratives from clinical notes.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 MedCaseAgent，一个即插即用的临床病例报告智能体，它将多模态基础模型与动态工具调用机制相结合，能够主动地从临床笔记中编排和综合复杂的临床叙述。

paragraphs.en: We introduce MedCase-150K , a large-scale collection of rare and novel disease clinical case reports, and MedCase-Bench , a temporally held-out subset derived from MedCase-150K, both designed for multimodal medical case report generation and rigorously stratified by clinical rarity.
paragraphs.zh: 我们介绍了 MedCase-150K，这是一个大规模的罕见病与新发疾病临床病例报告集合，以及 MedCase-Bench，一个从 MedCase-150K 中按时间留出的子集，二者均面向多模态医学病例报告生成设计，并按临床稀有程度进行了严格分层。

paragraphs.en: We validate MedCaseAgent comprehensively on MedCase-Bench, where it surpasses mainstream MLLMs and medical agentic systems. Clinician evaluations and a widespread user study further highlight the reliability and usefulness of MedCaseAgent.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在 MedCase-Bench 上对 MedCaseAgent 进行了全面验证，其表现超越了主流多模态大语言模型和医疗智能体系统。 临床医生评估和大规模用户研究进一步凸显了 MedCaseAgent 的可靠性与实用性。

paragraphs.en: Agentic Systems in Clinical Practice. Recent clinical agent research first shows strong progress in imaging. Across radiology and pathology, agentic systems support image-grounded reasoning ( Du et al., 2026 ; Qiu et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025a ) , evidence retrieval ( Cao et al., 2026 ) , report generation ( Qi et al., 2026 ; Zhong et al., 2025b ; Wang et al., 2026b ) , and quality control, but most remain designed for classification ( Fard et al., 2025 ) , segmentation ( Liu et al., 2026 ) , question answering ( He et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2024c ; Xiao et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2025b ; Jiang et al., 2025a ) , or planning ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) . Text-centered agents then extend these ideas to longitudinal records ( Li et al., 2025 ) , simulated hospital workflows ( Li et al., 2024b ) , clinical communication ( Zhi et al., 2025 ) , and safety oversight ( Kim et al., 2025 ) . Systems such as AgentEHR ( Liao et al., 2026 ) , MedAgentGym ( Xu et al., 2025a ) , and Reflectool ( Liao et al., 2025 ) study streaming EHRs ( Croxford et al., 2025 ) , retrospective summaries, and structured clinical tasks ( Ren et al., 2025 ; Zhong et al., 2025a ) . A related direction studies clinical diagnosis and agent architecture search with agentic reasoning systems ( Ghezloo et al., 2025 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ; Xia et al., 2025 ; Pushkar Mishra et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2025b ; Wu et al., 2025b ; Zhuang et al., 2025 ) . These methods improve traceability through retrieval ( Wang et al., 2026b ; Deng et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Rose et al., 2025 ; Ahmed et al., 2026 ) , verification ( Chen et al., 2025a ; Wang et al., 2026b ; Li et al., 2026 ; Ahmed et al., 2026 ) , and iterative refinement ( Chen et al., 2025a ; Wang et al., 2026b ; Li et al., 2026 ; Rose et al., 2025 ) , but usually stop at prediction ( Xia et al., 2025 ; Pushkar Mishra et al., 2025 ; Deng et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2025b ) , recommendation ( Wu et al., 2025b ) , or short-form clinical writing ( Wang et al., 2026b ) . By contrast, MedCaseAgent targets end-to-end case report synthesis, linking multimodal evidence, timeline reconstruction, literature support, and manuscript-level writing.

paragraphs.en: Automated Scientific and Case-Report Writing. General-purpose research-writing agents such as the AI Scientist ( Lu et al., 2024 ; Yamada et al., 2025 ) , data-to-paper ( Ifargan et al., 2024 ) , CycleResearcher ( Weng et al., 2024 ) , and PaperOrchestra ( Song et al., 2026 ) automate machine-learning or data-driven papers, but do not address patient-grounded clinical evidence, rarity assessment, or medical citation grounding. In medicine, prior studies prompted ChatGPT to draft individual case reports and concluded that the outputs required substantial expert revision and could contain fabricated references ( Buholayka et al., 2023 ; Pinto et al., 2024 ) ; case-report corpora have otherwise been used for diagnostic reasoning ( Wu et al., 2025a ) or information extraction ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) . MedCaseAgent instead treats case-report writing as a trainable, tool-grounded agentic task with a dedicated benchmark.
paragraphs.zh: 自动化科学研究与病例报告写作。 通用研究写作智能体（agents），例如 AI Scientist（Lu et al., 2024; Yamada et al., 2025）、data-to-paper（Ifargan et al., 2024）、CycleResearcher（Weng et al., 2024）和 PaperOrchestra（Song et al., 2026），实现了机器学习或数据驱动论文的自动化，但并未涉及基于患者的临床证据、罕见性评估或医学引用溯源。 在医学领域，已有研究提示 ChatGPT 起草单个病例报告，并得出结论认为其输出需要大量专家修订，且可能包含捏造的参考文献（Buholayka et al., 2023; Pinto et al., 2024）；此外，病例报告语料库还被用于诊断推理（Wu et al., 2025a）或信息抽取（Zhang et al., 2025b）。 MedCaseAgent 则将病例报告写作视为一项可训练的、以工具为基础的智能体任务，并配有专门的基准测试。

paragraphs.en: We first construct MedCase-150K, a large-scale collection of peer-reviewed clinical case reports. From this collection, we define MedCase-Bench as a temporally held-out evaluation subset of 584 case reports published after January 2026. MedCase-Bench will be open-sourced under CC-BY-NC 4.0. We then propose MedCaseAgent (Figure 1 ), an agentic report-writing system that plans over the fragmented evidence, retrieves supporting medical literature, drafts the manuscript, and audits the final report.
paragraphs.zh: 我们首先构建了 MedCase-150K，这是一个大规模的同行评审临床病例报告集合。 基于该集合，我们将 MedCase-Bench 定义为一个按时间划分的评测子集，包含 584 篇 2026 年 1 月之后发表的病例报告。 MedCase-Bench 将以 CC-BY-NC 4.0 许可证开源。 随后我们提出 MedCaseAgent（图 1），这是一个智能体化的报告撰写系统，能够对碎片化的证据进行规划、检索支持性的医学文献、起草稿件，并对最终报告进行审核。

paragraphs.en: Given unstructured clinical observations X X and external medical resources 𝒟 \mathcal{D} , the goal is to generate a structured clinical case report Y report Y_{\text{report}} . The inputs include textual clinical notes X notes = { x 1 , x 2 , … , x n } X_{\text{notes}}=\{x_{1},x_{2},\dots,x_{n}\} that describe patient demographics, symptoms, laboratory findings, diagnosis, treatment, and outcome, together with diagnostic images X img = { i 1 , i 2 , … , i m } X_{\text{img}}=\{i_{1},i_{2},\dots,i_{m}\} such as MRI, CT, radiography, or histology scans. We represent the textual input as clinical atoms grouped into history, presentation, diagnostics, management, and outcome. This atom format is designed to approximate the first-hand information that clinicians receive before a manuscript is written: partial notes, test results, image findings, missed visits, and follow-up details, rather than a polished academic narrative ( Abacha et al., 2023 ) . Recent work also suggests that LLM-written summaries can form portable representations for irregular clinical time series ( Ji et al., 2026 ) ; in our setting, atoms are used as controllable evidence for manuscript generation rather than as predictive embeddings. The atom format also gives a stable supervision unit for planner training and reward computation, since each generated plan can be checked for atom coverage. The target output is a complete report with source-driven manuscript sections such as Introduction, Case Description, Discussion, and References. During generation, the vision-language model acts as an agent. It issues tool calls and search queries q t q_{t} to retrieve supporting knowledge Z retrieved Z_{\text{retrieved}} from 𝒟 \mathcal{D} , and then links the raw clinical atoms with a complete manuscript. Figure 2 illustrates fragmented and partially structured clinical observations as the multimodal input for MedCaseAgent; Appendix B provides a fuller prompt-output atom-compression view.

paragraphs.en: While datasets like CaseReportBench ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) treat case reports as targets for information extraction, our setting requires a model to write a complete, well-cited report from fragmented multimodal inputs, which is a much harder problem. As there is no existing dataset for this domain, we construct MedCase-150K, a dataset of 154,872 case reports describing rare diseases and unprecedented or atypical presentations (see Appendix C , Data Construction and Validation, for dataset overview and statistics). Each MedCase-150K entry contains a published source article, unpaired medical images, and the corresponding LLM-compressed clinical atoms. The construction pipeline of MedCase-150K is semi-automated. First, we manually identify PMC Open Access case-report publications with full-text XML and high-quality medical images. An LLM-based parser converts the final prose into unstructured clinical atoms X notes X_{\text{notes}} by removing background literature, reference-driven claims, and final diagnostic exposition. The parser keeps patient-specific facts, including timeline details, tests, treatments, image findings, and outcomes.

The Disease-Index RAG corpus excludes the evaluated cases’ source articles and related literature to prevent information leakage. paragraphs.en: We train the phase 1 planner with a two-stage recipe implemented with SWIFT and LoRA adapters. Figure 4 summarizes the planner-training flow from multimodal inputs through SFT trajectories and GRPO reward feedback. This use of supervised trajectories followed by verifiable reward feedback follows the GRPO-style reasoning-training line ( Shao et al., 2024 ) and is aligned with recent medical reasoning work on verifiable problems, process supervision, and reinforcement learning ( Chen et al., 2025b ; Jiang et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2025a ) . First, we apply supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on teacher-generated planner trajectories. paragraphs.en: Evaluation metrics. We evaluate generated reports from complementary views. Rubric-level judge scores assess citation depth, patient-history nuance, clinical coherence, image integration, and readability on a 0–10 scale; we linearly scale them to 0–100 for display and report average quality as the mean of these five dimensions. Disease-subset scores test robustness across common, rare, and ultra-rare diagnoses; rule-based metrics audit retrieval, novelty recognition, figure ordering, and citation coverage; and clinician-reviewer A/B validation measures practical preference and authorship indistinguishability.

paragraphs.en: Table 2 reports rule-based and structural metrics for source retrieval, novelty recognition, figure ordering, authorship indistinguishability, and citation coverage. Exact DOI measures whether a keyword-based literature search retrieves the ground-truth PubMed source paper from which the atoms were derived. Note that even if the ground-truth paper is retrieved, it is masked during report generation to prevent information leakage. Exact DOI is thus a per-case source-retrieval hit rate: it reflects whether the agent’s queries are specific enough to surface the single article describing the same patient among millions of PubMed records. Novelty Recognition is the percentage of cases where the model recognizes rare or first-case novelty even though this cue is omitted from the atoms. Figure Sequence Accuracy is binary per case: 1 only when the generated report uses the same figure order as the published reference, and 0 otherwise. Authorship Indistinguishability follows an LLM-based A/B test and measures how often generated reports are difficult to distinguish from the published ones. Inspired by PaperOrchestra ( Song et al., 2026 ) , we assess citation coverage using two reference tiers. P0 denotes must-cite analogous or claim-critical case-report sources. P1 denotes useful background, mechanism, treatment, or comparison sources. After canonical PubMed/DOI/title matching, tier k k is scored as Recall k = | C ∩ G k | / | G k | \mathrm{Recall}_{k}=|C\cap G_{k}|/|G_{k}| , where C C is the generated citation set and G k G_{k} is the reference set for that tier. MedCaseAgent-Max has the strongest structural grounding (84.59% Exact DOI vs. 46.90% for the strongest direct baseline), the best novelty recognition, the closest figure sequencing, and the highest P0/P1 Recall.

paragraphs.en: To assess whether MedCaseAgent can support case-report writing from real clinical data, we conducted a hospital-based study using 30 de-identified multimodal cases from 10 hospitals. All cases were selected as suitable for rare-disease case-report preparation, including cases with unpublished manuscripts intended for submission. Fourteen clinical experts assessed reports generated from raw records and report-derived atoms alongside clinician-written reports; each case was independently reviewed by three experts against the source records. Table 4 shows comparable overall quality for raw-record and atom-based generation (7.4 versus 7.6), with higher omission-control scores for raw input (7.8 versus 7.6). Appendix F.1 details the input differences. Because these cases have no published source article, they evaluate MedCaseAgent in its intended deployment setting. In a paired calibration, LLM judgments agreed with clinicians in 23–26 of 30 assessments across scored dimensions (quadratic-weighted κ \kappa = 0.69–0.76; ICC = 0.69–0.77) and in all 30 hallucination checks (Appendix F.2 ).

paragraphs.en: We presented MedCaseAgent, a planner–writer–editor agent that turns fragmented clinical notes and medical images into publication-style rare-disease case reports, together with MedCase-150K and MedCase-Bench, a 584-case temporal holdout of reports published after the construction cutoff. Tool-grounded planning yields large gains in verifiable grounding: MedCaseAgent-Max retrieves the exact source article for 84.6% of cases against 46.9% for the strongest direct baseline, recognizes case novelty in 88.4% of cases, and attains the highest must-cite citation recall. It is the best-performing system on every disease subset, from COVID-19 to ultra-rare diseases, and scores above the human-publication reference under a four-judge ensemble spanning four model families. In blinded review, experienced clinicians more often preferred MedCaseAgent reports over the published originals, and most did not consistently identify which report was generated. The remaining frontier is diseases with no precedent in the retrieval sources: there, MedCaseAgent can organize the available evidence and its uncertainty, but the discovery is the clinician’s.

paragraphs.en: Recent benchmarks for clinical agents can be grouped by what they evaluate. One group studies clinical reasoning and decision making, including HealthBench ( Arora et al., 2025 ) , MedAgentBench ( Jiang et al., 2025b ) , MedConsultBench ( Qiao et al., 2026 ) , ClinDEF ( Tang et al., 2025 ) , VivaBench ( Chiu et al., 2025 ) , RareBench ( Chen et al., 2024a ) , and MedAgentBoard ( Zhu et al., 2025b ) . A second group focuses on multimodal, imaging-centered, or sequential clinical decision-making evaluation, such as ReX-MLE ( Kenia et al., 2025 ) , MedicalNarratives ( Ikezogwo et al., 2025 ) , AgentClinic ( Schmidgall et al., 2024 ) , and MTBBench ( Vasilev et al., 2025 ) . A third group targets clinical workflow, dialogue, and system-level behavior, including MedBench ( Cai et al., 2024 ) , 3mdbench ( Sviridov et al., 2025 ) , Care-bench ( Wang et al., 2026a ) , and MMRareBench ( Ning et al., 2026 ) . Other benchmarks examine safety, privacy, and structured extraction, such as MedPriv-Bench ( Guan et al., 2026 ) , MedRiskEval ( Corbeil et al., 2026 ) , and ClinBench ( Villanueva Miranda et al., 2026 ) . PMC-Patients ( Zhao et al., 2023 ) provides patient summaries for patient and literature retrieval, while RareArena ( Chen et al., 2026 ) benchmarks rare-disease diagnosis. Despite this growing benchmark ecosystem, most existing settings still focus on question answering, information extraction, summarization, diagnosis, report evaluation, or simulated interaction. Clinical case report generation brings these abilities together in a single task. A strong system must interpret fragmented multimodal evidence, reconstruct the patient course, link findings to prior literature, and write a rigorous scientific narrative.

paragraphs.en: During MedCase-Bench construction, 23 PhD researchers and domain experts with medical or biomedical backgrounds manually reviewed all 632 candidate cases. Each case was independently reviewed by at least two experts, with pre-adjudication judgments retained. paragraphs.en: Rare disease status is not always a stable binary property: the prevalence, clinical significance, and publication novelty of a condition can change across time, geography, and medical context. For publications identified as case reports, we assign one of four rarity labels. rare_disease means that the underlying disease or condition is epidemiologically rare. unprecedented_presentation means that the report describes a first-of-its-kind or completely novel manifestation. atypical_presentation means that a known disease appears in an uncommon form, location, demographic group, or clinical context. standard_case means that the report is a useful teaching case but does not contain a major rare-disease or novel-presentation element. For stratified corpus views, rare_disease , unprecedented_presentation , and atypical_presentation are grouped as rare or novelty-bearing case reports, while standard_case is retained as the non-rare/non-novel comparison group.

paragraphs.en: The tuned MedCaseAgent planner reported in the experiments is initialized from Qwen3.5-9B and trained with a two-stage SFT-to-GRPO recipe using the SWIFT training stack. The planner training set contains 3,000 phase-1 planning trajectories derived from the MedCase-150K training split. These trajectories are generated by a Qwen3.5-397B-A17B teacher planner: for each case, the teacher reads the compressed clinical atoms and mapped images, issues image-analysis and literature-search actions, records public tool observations, builds an evidence table with DOI-linked citations, and writes the final section-level case-report plan. The data-preparation step converts each teacher trace into SWIFT agent messages and removes private thinking fields. For the GRPO and evaluation records, source DOI identifiers are kept only as scorer-side labels; if search hits the source article for a case, its title, abstract, and article text are masked from policy-visible observations, while non-source PubMed records remain available as retrieved support.
paragraphs.zh: 实验中报告的经过调优的 MedCaseAgent 智能体规划器以 Qwen3.5-9B 初始化，并使用 SWIFT 训练框架，通过“SFT 到 GRPO”的两阶段方案进行训练。 智能体规划器训练集包含 3000 条来自 MedCase-150K 训练划分的第一阶段规划轨迹。 这些轨迹由 Qwen3.5-397B-A17B 教师规划器生成：对于每个病例，教师读取压缩后的临床原子信息和映射图像，执行图像分析和文献检索动作，记录公开的工具观测结果，构建带有 DOI 链接引用的证据表，并撰写最终的章节级病例报告规划。 数据准备步骤将每条教师轨迹转换为 SWIFT 智能体消息，并移除私有的思考字段。 对于 GRPO 和评估记录，源 DOI 标识符仅作为评分端标签保留；如果检索命中了某病例的源文章，其标题、摘要和正文会从策略可见的观测中遮蔽，而非源 PubMed 记录则仍作为检索到的支持材料保持可用。

paragraphs.en: We retrospectively assembled 30 original, non-public, de-identified multimodal cases from 10 hospitals through an ongoing case-report effort coordinated by the authors’ institution under existing IRB approval. Each case involved a rare or clinically complex presentation and included longitudinal clinical records, multimodal evidence, and a corresponding report prepared and reviewed by the clinical team. These reports included both published articles and complete unpublished manuscripts prepared for submission. Cases were selected for sufficiently complete records and a matched clinician-written report; consolidating records across hospitals and care episodes required clinical coordination and manual review. All materials were de-identified before analysis.
paragraphs.zh: 我们通过作者所在机构在既有伦理审查委员会（IRB）批准下协调开展的一项持续进行的病例报告工作，回顾性汇集了来自10家医院的30个原创、非公开、已去标识化的多模态病例。 每个病例均涉及罕见或临床上复杂的临床表现，并包含纵向临床记录、多模态证据以及由临床团队撰写并审阅的相应报告。 这些报告既包括已发表的文章，也包括为投稿而撰写的完整未发表稿件。 病例入选的标准是记录足够完整且有一份匹配的临床医生撰写的报告；跨医院和跨诊疗阶段的记录整合需要临床协调和人工审阅。 所有材料在分析前均已去标识化。

paragraphs.en: For each patient, MedCaseAgent generated one report directly from the raw clinical records ( E raw E_{\mathrm{raw}} ) and another from report-derived clinical atoms ( E atom E_{\mathrm{atom}} ). The atoms were obtained by compressing the clinician-written manuscript, rather than by directly extracting facts from the raw clinical files; images were supplied separately without captions or explicit atom-level links. Experts compared both generated reports with the clinician-written report and used the original records to verify patient facts. Raw records contained redundancy, irregular timelines, uncertainty, and cross-source conflicts, requiring filtering, deduplication, source reconciliation, and timeline reconstruction. Report-derived atoms retained the core history, examinations, treatment, and follow-up in a more concise form, but compressed some source context.
paragraphs.zh: 对于每位患者，MedCaseAgent 直接从原始临床记录（E_raw）生成一份报告，并从报告衍生的临床原子（E_atom）生成另一份报告。 这些原子是通过对临床医生撰写的文稿进行压缩获得的，而不是直接从原始临床文件中提取事实；图像单独提供，不带图注，也没有显式的原子级链接。 专家将两份生成的报告与临床医生撰写的报告进行比较，并使用原始记录核实患者事实。 原始记录包含冗余、不规则的时间线、不确定性以及跨来源的冲突，需要进行过滤、去重、来源核对和时间线重建。 报告衍生的原子以更简洁的形式保留了核心病史、检查、治疗和随访内容，但压缩了部分来源背景信息。

paragraphs.en: Fourteen clinical experts assessed the 30 cases, with every case independently reviewed by three experts. Experts assessed overall report quality, patient-timeline reconstruction, and omission control on a 1–10 scale, with higher scores indicating better performance, while checking the reports against the source records. Table 4 reports the mean scores for raw-record generation, atom-based generation, and clinician-written reports.

paragraphs.en: In the order of overall quality, patient timeline, and omission control, mean scores were 7.4/7.5/7.8 for raw-record generation, 7.6/7.6/7.6 for atom-based generation, and 7.5/7.8/7.9 for clinician-written reports. paragraphs.en: Because claims about medical AI value require evidence that goes beyond technical performance alone (“Show us the evidence for the value of medical AI”, 2026 ), we tested whether automatic gains translate into real manuscript-review value through a blinded A/B study. In this study, 32 expert clinicians (with at least 5 years of review experience in clinical case reports) each reviewed five paired cases, yielding 160 pairwise judgments. In each pair, the clinician saw the same de-identified case context and images, a MedCaseAgent-Max report and the corresponding published reference in randomized order, then judged authorship and selected the stronger case report. We summarize source-identification consistency at the reviewer level by counting clinicians who correctly identify the generated report in at most three of five pairs. Under this criterion, 26 of 32 clinicians (81.3%) did not consistently identify report sources across their five assigned pairs; reviewers also more often selected MedCaseAgent as the stronger manuscript.
paragraphs.zh: 由于关于医疗AI价值的论断需要超越单纯技术性能的证据（“请展示医疗AI价值的证据”，2026），我们通过一项盲法A/B研究检验了自动化的增益能否转化为真实的稿件评审价值。 在本研究中，32名专家临床医生（在临床病例报告领域拥有至少5年评审经验）各自评审了五组配对病例，共产生160个成对判断。 在每一组配对中，临床医生会看到相同的去标识化病例背景与图像、一份MedCaseAgent-Max报告及对应的已发表参考文献（顺序随机），随后判断报告的作者归属并选出更优的病例报告。 我们通过统计在五组配对中最多仅在不超过三组中正确识别出生成报告的临床医生人数，在评审者层面总结来源识别的一致性。 在此标准下，32名临床医生中有26名（81.3%）在其被分配的五组配对中未能一致地识别出报告来源；评审者还更常选择MedCaseAgent生成的稿件为更优稿件。

paragraphs.en: The paired cases are drawn from the post-January-2026 evaluation split, and report source labels are hidden from reviewers. Reviewers may also enter optional 1–5 rubric scores and free-text comments on hallucination, image interpretation, and overall quality. We report only aggregate statistics and omit reviewer identifiers, raw comments, and patient-level content.

paragraphs.en: Table G1 extends the MedCaseAgent-Max-vs.-reference comparison reported with human judges in Appendix F.3 to all baseline systems, using an ensemble of four LLM judges (Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, Claude Opus 4.6) under the same blinded-A/B protocol with hidden model names, randomized A/B order, and evidence-grounded rationales ( Liu et al., 2023 ; Zheng et al., 2023 ) . The ensemble enables coverage across all baselines at a scale that would be infeasible with clinicians. Paired LLM–clinician agreement is reported separately in Appendix F.2 . MedCaseAgent-Max is the least often identified as generated ( 63.91 % 63.91\% ) and the most often preferred over the reference ( 64.26 % 64.26\% ), with MedCaseAgent-Base and MedCaseAgent-Tuned showing stepwise gains over the non-agentic baselines. The clinician study complements this automatic table: most expert reviewers fail to recover MedCaseAgent’s source labels across a full blinded review round while still finding the generated manuscripts useful, supporting the claim that the system is strong under automatic evaluation and persuasive in clinical review.

paragraphs.en: MedCaseAgent is intended to support clinicians in writing case reports. Case-report writing is a time-consuming part of clinical knowledge sharing: clinicians must organize patient history, diagnostic evidence, images, treatment course, outcomes, and related literature before a report can be submitted. Unlike open-ended research-paper generation, this writing task is strongly evidence-based and grounded in an observed patient case, making it well suited to a clinician-controlled tool that structures evidence rather than inventing new claims.
paragraphs.zh: MedCaseAgent 旨在支持临床医生撰写病例报告。 病例报告的撰写是临床知识共享中耗时的环节：在报告提交之前，临床医生必须整理患者病史、诊断证据、影像资料、治疗过程、结局以及相关文献。 与开放式的科研论文生成不同，这项写作任务高度以证据为基础，并扎根于一个被观察到的患者病例，因此非常适合一个由临床医生掌控、负责组织证据而非编造新论断的智能体工具。

paragraphs.en: The main positive impact is therefore to reduce the documentation and literature-review burden involved in manuscript preparation. MedCaseAgent helps organize fragmented notes, medical images, prior-case evidence, and citation candidates into a structured draft that remains available for expert review. This support is especially useful for rare, atypical, or unprecedented presentations, where clinicians must compare a complex patient course against sparse prior literature.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，主要的好处是减轻稿件撰写过程中涉及的文档整理与文献综述负担。 MedCaseAgent 有助于将零散的笔记、医学影像、既往病例证据和引用候选文献整理成结构化的草稿，供专家审阅时使用。 这种支持对于罕见、非典型或前所未有的病例表现尤为有用，因为临床医生必须将复杂的患者病程与稀少的既往文献进行对比。

paragraphs.en: MedCaseAgent may also provide useful cues before writing begins. During the planning stage, retrieval over analogous cases, literature, images, and disease-level evidence can help surface diagnostic possibilities or comparative context that clinicians may want to consider. These planning outputs are not meant to replace expert diagnosis, but they can serve as organized signals for specialists who are already evaluating a difficult case. More broadly, the system may enable faster dissemination of rare-disease observations, more consistent case-report structure, and broader participation from clinical teams with limited time for manuscript drafting.
paragraphs.zh: MedCaseAgent 也可以在写作开始之前提供有用的提示。 在规划阶段，对相似病例、文献、影像和疾病层面证据的检索，可以帮助显现临床医生可能希望考虑的诊断可能性或对比性背景信息。 这些规划输出并非旨在取代专家诊断，但它们可以作为有组织的信号，提供给正在评估疑难病例的专科医生。 更广泛地说，该系统可能有助于更快地传播罕见病观察结果，使病例报告结构更加一致，并让时间有限、难以撰写稿件的临床团队更广泛地参与进来。

paragraphs.en: Responsible use should keep clinicians at the center of the workflow. Patient facts, image interpretations, and citation support should be verified before submission or dissemination, and any deployment on real clinical records should follow local governance, consent, de-identification, and access-control requirements.
paragraphs.zh: 负责任的使用应让临床医生始终处于工作流程的中心。 患者事实、影像解读和引用支持应在提交或传播之前加以核实，任何在真实临床记录上的部署都应遵循当地的治理、知情同意、去标识化和访问控制要求。

paragraphs.en: This disclosure concerns LLMs as the modeling technology studied in this work, including the agentic planner, writer, editor, and LLM-judge evaluation components described in the main paper. Separate from the method, LLM-based tools were used only for manuscript writing and editing assistance. They were not used to fabricate patient records, experimental measurements, baselines, or evaluation outcomes; final reported numbers must be produced by the evaluation pipeline and be traceable to released scripts, prompts, and logs.
paragraphs.zh: 本公开内容涉及作为本工作所研究建模技术的大语言模型，包括主论文中描述的智能体规划器、写作器、编辑器以及大语言模型评审等评估组件。 与方法本身无关，基于大语言模型的工具仅用于论文写作和编辑辅助。 它们未被用于伪造患者记录、实验测量结果、基线方法或评估结果；最终报告的数字必须由评估流程生成，并能够追溯至公开的脚本、提示词和日志。
